messages:
maria: Heads-up — we've been seeing a slow uptick in Xid 63/ECC spikes across a handful of SXM2 nodes in eu-west-1 over the past 48h. Alerting threshold hit for 3 racks in the same cluster. 

samir: I noticed it too. Error pattern looks intermittent, cards still pass basic checks but errors spike under 90-150 token gen load.

josh: Which racks? any common serials/batch ids?

maria: racks h14, h17, h18. Pulling provisioning metadata now. Early hint: same vendor PO and lot shipped Q4 last year.

kevin: Can you paste the error snippet?

maria: Sure — from node h14-03: 
```
[GPU0] Xid 63 2026-03-16T22:14:07Z ECC_UNCORRECTABLE / nv_peer_mem:?
[GPU0] GPU ECC 0x2c at 0x7ff...
```

ashley: Xid 63 usually points at PCIe/host comm or memory. But seeing ECC on single card under mid-load suggests contact or power rail issue.

samir: I ran the quick health playbook: `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,PERF` nothing obvious; `smartd` for the NVMe hosts is fine. I toggled power-cycle on h14-03 and error stopped for ~6 hours, then returned.

josh: Intermittent stop/start recovery + cluster-localized -> suspect connector/contact degradation (SXM retention/guide pins), especially if lot was same manufacturing date.

maria: I pulled the inventory: 8 cards across the 3 racks share serial prefix NV-LTQ-9. Vendor confirmed batch code 2112-B.

kevin: Let's not do mass RMA yet. Proposal: schedule a small bench test: remove one suspect card, replicate load on bench with monitored humidity and torque adjustments, try reseating + isopropyl swab of SXM contact. Record before/after Xid counts.

ashley: Agreed. Also add a short-term mitigation in infra: auto-drain nodes when per-card Xid63 rate > 5/min over 15m and fallback to sibling pool. Right now our drain threshold is 10/min. Lowering will reduce customer impact.

maria: Action items: 
- josh: pick two cards (h14-03 and h17-01) for bench by EOD.
- kevin: update alert runbook & lower threshold to 5/min for the cluster (will roll config).
- samir: schedule maintenance window for reseat+inspection and mark nodes for careful redeploy.

josh: On it. I'll also grab a microscope photo of SXM lip and retention screws torque. If we see oxidation/corrosion that's telling.

infra-bot: deploy-config change requested by kevin queued. CI job: infra/alerts/cluster-xid-threshold -> new_threshold=5.

kevin: infra-bot — please include a temporary suppression rule to avoid alert storms while we repair nodes.

infra-bot: suppression rule added for cluster eu-west-1 for 4h.

maria: Quick bench results (update): h14-03 when run in bench with 95% duty cycle for 3 hours produced reproducible Xid spikes. After reseat + cleaned contact with IPA + torque to spec, errors went away for 1.5h under same load; after simulated vibration (gentle tap) errors returned. Microscope photo shows minor greenish residue on one corner of the SXM carrier.

josh: That matches connector corrosion/film. Vendor notes: some lots shipped with insufficient conformal coating on carrier edges in humid conditions. I'll open case.

rma-bot: Vendor case opened: case# RMA-6421, priority P2. Vendor requested serials and bench logs.

kevin: Good. Short-term plan: 1) Replace the 8 affected cards in the 3 racks with spares from reserve pool 2) Update node drain threshold 3) Add humidity sensor to rack h14 and h17 4) Expand burn-in test to include 48h mixed-load +/- vibration on incoming SXM cards.

ashley: Cost note: replacing 8 cards from spare pool will reduce available capacity; estimate 12% throughput hit in eu-west-1 for 24-48h. Finance flagged excess RMA costs if vendor refuses warranty. We should document the lot and pursue chargeback.

maria: I'll draft an internal postmortem and include timeline, bench evidence, photos, and vendor correspondence. Draft will include a new hardware acceptance checklist item for visual inspection and humidity-stamp verification.

samir: Also let's add a telemetry metric for per-card reseat_count and last_reseat_timestamp so we can correlate future parity.

josh: For the immediate replacement: I'll coordinate with ops for hot-swap windows. Nodes to be drained with: 
```
kubectl drain node/ip-10-234-41-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
ssh ops@h14-shelf3 'powercycle gpu-slot2'
```

maria: Timeline: replace tonight window 0200-0600 UTC for 3 racks. I'll post the change on #incidents and notify customers with impacted SLAs via support.

kevin: Postmortem checklist: root cause = connector corrosion on SXM carrier from specific lot, contributing factors = rack humidity spike (AC transient) + lack of visual inspection on acceptance. Fixes = replace affected cards, update burn-in and acceptance, add humidity sensors, lower alert thresholds, add reseat telemetry, pursue warranty RMA.

ashley: Assigning owners in the doc: vendor engagement (josh), fleet replacements (maria), alerting/runbook (kevin), ops scheduling (samir), finance follow-up (ashley).

maria: Thanks all. I'll attach photos + bench logs to the PM. Will follow up with root-cause writeup and pubsub to #all-hands after vendor conclusion. :white_check_mark:
